# SK3021 — A `SpinLock` is stored in a `readonly` field

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A field of type `System.Threading.SpinLock` is declared `readonly`, so every caller takes the lock on a defensive copy.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Async |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, review it |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| ReSharper | `SpinLockInReadonlyField` (`resharper_spin_lock_in_readonly_field_highlighting`) |

## Why

`SpinLock` is a mutable struct and its state *is* the lock. `Enter` is not a `readonly` member, so reading a `readonly` field to call it makes the compiler take a defensive copy: the lock is acquired on a temporary and released on a temporary, and nothing is ever excluded. It compiles, it runs, `lockTaken` comes back true every time, and the race the lock was written to prevent is exactly as it was — with the code above it saying otherwise. Removing `readonly` is the only repair.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
sealed class Counter {
    readonly SpinLock gate = new(false);

    int value;

    public void Increment() {
        var taken = false;
        gate.Enter(ref taken);
        value++;
        if (taken) {
            gate.Exit();
        }
    }
}
```

Write:

```csharp
sealed class Counter {
    SpinLock gate = new(false);

    int value;

    public void Increment() {
        var taken = false;
        gate.Enter(ref taken);
        value++;
        if (taken) {
            gate.Exit();
        }
    }
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **The fix is one word and it is not cosmetic.** Removing `readonly` makes the field assignable and makes every call site operate on the real lock instead of a copy, which changes what the program does — for the better, and still not without review. `fixIsSafe` is false for that reason rather than because the edit is uncertain: there is exactly one repair and no intent to guess at. ⚠ The type is resolved by the semantic model and never matched on the written name: `SpinLock` is a plausible name for somebody's own type and stripping `readonly` from a field of one would be a change made for no reason. ⚠ **One finding per declaration, not per declarator.** `readonly SpinLock a, b;` has one `readonly` token, and two findings would carry the same deletion twice. ⚠ **An instance field inside a `readonly struct` is the same bug and is withheld, because the fix would not compile.** CS8340 requires every instance field of a `readonly struct` to be `readonly`, so the keyword there is not the author's choice and deleting it is an error rather than a repair; the lock is just as broken, and the repair is to stop the containing type being a `readonly struct`, which is a design change and not an edit. The same applies to a `SpinLock` returned from a property or exposed through an `in` parameter.
